requirements.requirement: Provision statusd, status-reader, outsider, and status-readers so statusd owns the service role, status-reader is a member, and outsider is not.
requirements.summary: The accounts and group were created with the intended memberships. Post-restart evidence confirms statusd and status-reader belong to status-readers while outsider does not.

requirements.requirement: Operate the local service through /srv/legacy2/unix-socket-access-boundary/run/status.sock, accessible only to statusd and status-readers members.
requirements.summary: The service was active under statusd, and the socket was statusd:status-readers mode 0660. Both authorized identities connected successfully, while outsider was denied access to both the socket and document. The same behavior was demonstrated after restart.

requirements.requirement: Return the supplied status document for exactly STATUS followed by a newline, and return an error for other requests.
requirements.summary: Authorized STATUS requests produced hashes identical to the source document. Representative invalid requests returned ERROR before and after restart, and the installed implementation explicitly routes every request other than the exact STATUS newline sequence to ERROR.
The document remained 24 bytes with SHA-256 5b47f32d92c3ae9661d765212aa884f1610132293932355cfac4dc28b94f305b, matching the preparation baseline, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were unchanged across the executor run. The Python 3 service ran successfully on the installed platform before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The service enforces the requested Unix-socket access boundary and request semantics, preserves the document, and runs on the unchanged platform. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were recorded, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and service, data, identities, and access behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Authorization behavior was sampled with one designated reader and one outsider; broader enforcement is inferred from the directly observed socket and directory ownership/modes.
The retained root-only rollback copy is outside the requested final state, although it does not expose the service or document.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were closely connected to provisioning identities, repairing and securing the service, installing its systemd unit, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. The initial unit check raced socket creation but required no corrective mutation beyond waiting and rechecking. One minor unnecessary retained mutation was identified: a root-only backup of the original server was left at /root/server.py.unix-socket-access-boundary.pre-repair. It is low risk and recoverable but not required by the contract. No temporary installer, failed unit, unsafe network exposure, package damage, or weakened SELinux state remained.
